Reportedly, Apple has significantly increased its vapor chamber orders, indicating that this cooling technology may play a more important role in its future hardware product line. Here are the details.

Apple doubles down on vapor chamber cooling technology

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital posted on Weibo that Apple has "significantly increased its total vapor chamber orders," and suggested this move "may be to prepare enhanced cooling for its first foldable iPhone and the next-generation 20th anniversary model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling technology on the iPhone 17 Pro, a change that helped address thermal issues that had persisted across several previous generations.

Vapor chambers work by evaporating a small amount of liquid near the heat source, then condensing it at a cooler location to disperse the heat over a larger area before allowing the liquid to flow back and repeat the cycle.

You can see the entire process for yourself in this excellent video from Know Art below:

Although the Weibo post speculates that Apple's increased procurement this time is for the iPhone Ultra and the rumored 20th anniversary iPhone expected in 2027, based on timing, it is more reasonable for this year's product lineup to adopt the technology.

According to reports, Apple has asked suppliers to prepare approximately 10 million foldable iPhones, an increase from the earlier target of 7 to 8 million units, while stockpiling around 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling technology.

The order increase comes amid reports that Apple has resolved earlier hinge and production yield issues, paving the way for ramping up output ahead of a September launch.
